title: dumpex v2 structured output (schema_version 2.12)
description: Validates the v2 envelope written by the six recon commands (--list/--modules/--threads/--pid/--sysinfo/--peb), --diff, --extract, --strings, --report, and --hunt, via --json. v2.9 added `investigation_actions` to `huntSummary` (result.summary for kind == "hunt") -- the deduplicated, priority-ordered skipped-target investigation queue `--hunt all` builds automatically from already-collected coverage metadata (see the `investigationAction` $def and dumpex.hunt._investigation.build_investigation_queue()). v2.10 adds `content_reason_codes` to `triageInfo`: the opt-in `--hunt all --triage-skipped` budgeted deep-content triage pass (dumpex.hunt._deep_triage.run_deep_triage(), issue #19 Phase 2) reuses --report's own low-level content-scan primitive under an explicit per-target/whole-run/target-count budget and records what it actually found (an IOC-pattern string match, a network-pattern string match, a bare MZ header, and/or an MZ header CONFIRMED to sit in unregistered/unbacked memory) as this new closed-enum array -- always `[]` for the default `mode == "metadata"` pass. `investigation_actions` remains always present and `[]` for a single-hunter `--hunt <name>` run; populated only for `selected == "all"`. v2.11 adds `va`/`region_offset`/`file_offset` to `huntPeHeaderHit`: `--hunt injection`'s hidden-PE scan now searches each eligible region for candidate 'MZ' headers at every byte offset instead of only probing the region base (https://github.com/bitbug0x55AA/dumpex/issues/26), so a hit's containing region no longer identifies where the PE actually is -- these three fields carry the candidate's own process address, its offset inside that region, and its .dmp file offset (`null` when the VA is not covered by a captured segment). They are required and always emitted; for a PE at a region's base `va` equals `region.base_address` and `region_offset` is 0. v2.12 (https://github.com/bitbug0x55AA/dumpex/issues/28): `coverageLimitation.targets` is no longer exclusive to SCAN_REGION_OVERSIZED_SKIPPED -- PE_HEADER_READ_FAILED/PE_HEADER_SHORT_READ/PE_HEADER_SCAN_TRUNCATED/PE_HEADER_SCAN_NOT_STARTED (injection's hidden-PE scan) and SCAN_REGION_READ_FAILED/SCAN_REGION_SHORT_READ (pipe/cs-beacon/yara/obfuscation/stomping's region and segment scans, and any other hunter using the shared CoverageTracker) may now carry a `targets` array too, identifying the exact region a read failed/read short/was truncated/was never started on rather than only counting it -- OPTIONAL on these six codes (still `[]` when a producer cannot resolve target identity), and when non-empty its length must equal `affected_count`. PE_HEADER_SCAN_NOT_STARTED is a new code distinguishing a LATER region the whole-hunt scan budget was already exhausted before its own search ever started (nothing examined at all) from PE_HEADER_SCAN_TRUNCATED's own claim (this region's own search got PART of it before running out of budget -- an unfinished remainder). `scanTarget.size_limit` is now nullable: `null` for a target that was never actually oversized (a read-failed/short-read/scan-truncated/not-started target has no cap it exceeded), non-null only for an oversized-skip target. `skipRelationship` (inside `investigationAction`) gains a required `cause` field (`"oversized_skipped"`/`"read_failed"`/`"short_read"`/`"scan_truncated"`/`"scan_not_started"`) -- `hunter`/`source`/`scope` alone cannot distinguish these, and `build_investigation_queue()` now dedups on the four together; `skipRelationship.size_limit` is correspondingly nullable, non-null only when `cause` is `"oversized_skipped"`. Later same-version additions (issue #28 P4 follow-up, still schema_version 2.12): PE_HEADER_SCAN_TRUNCATED/PE_HEADER_SCAN_NOT_STARTED may optionally set `scope` to the hidden-PE scan budget (reads_per_region/total_bytes/validations_per_region/validations_total) that stopped the affected region(s), with `detail` ("limit=<int> consumed=<int>") carrying that budget's own configured limit and how much was consumed; `build_investigation_queue()`'s dedup key drops `ScanTarget.kind` (a memory_region and a memory_segment target naming the same (base_address, size) now merge into one investigation_actions entry, enriching a segment-only representative with MemoryInfo facts from the already-passed memory_regions when a covering region exists).

evidence.description: One entry per evidence source. A single-dump recon command emits exactly one entry (role: 'primary'); a comparison command emits one per side (e.g. 'baseline'/'target').

rules.description: rules.yaml provenance for this run -- matches dumpex.rules_pkg.loader.get_rules_source_info()'s return shape. Omitted entirely (not present as a key at all) when get_rules() was never called this run (e.g. --hunt injection alone never reads rules.yaml) -- see dumpex.output.envelope._rules_meta. `path`/`sha256` are only null for the built-in defaults (no file was loaded at all); `path` is basename-only under --redact-paths, matching every other path-bearing meta field's own redaction rule. `version` has no lower bound -- rules_pkg.loader only type-checks a rules.yaml-declared `version:` field, never its sign (see loader.py's own _validate_top_level), so this schema does not invent a constraint the Python side doesn't enforce. `path == null` is EXACTLY the built-in-defaults shape (dumpex.rules_pkg.loader's own hardcoded fallback dict, verified against _load_rules()'s only path==None assignment) -- sha256/explicit/version are pinned to null/false/1 on that branch, not merely nullable.

yara_rules.description: YARA rule-file provenance for this run -- matches dumpex.hunt.yara_hunt.get_yara_provenance()'s return shape. Omitted entirely when YARA scanning was never invoked this run (e.g. --hunt injection alone never loads any .yar/.yara file) -- see dumpex.output.envelope._yara_rules_meta. `rules_dir` is basename-only under --redact-paths. `aggregate_sha256` is never null in this branch -- load_and_compile() always calls hashlib.sha256().hexdigest() unconditionally (even over zero rule files), which never returns null; only the error-only branch below omits it entirely.

hexAddress.description: A memory address/pointer/handle, normalized to a fixed-width (16 hex digit), lowercase, 0x-prefixed string -- or null when there is nothing to report an address for (see dumpex/output/records.py's hex_address()). Never a bare int (uint64 precision isn't safe across all JSON consumers) and never a variable-width string.

module_context.description: resolved: backed by a known module. unregistered: ModuleListStream was available and this address is confirmed NOT backed by any known module (a real DFIR signal). unavailable: ModuleListStream itself is missing -- can't tell either way, must not be confused with 'unregistered'. null: start_address is itself unknown (module context is moot).

extractRecord.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.ExtractRecord.to_dict() -- the READ-side facts for one --extract invocation. `requested_address`/`requested_size` are never null -- a successful --extract always knows the exact address/size it read (unlike most other hexAddress-typed fields in this schema, which stay nullable for genuinely optional cases). NOT expressed here (Python-only, see ExtractRecord.__post_init__): bytes_read must never exceed requested_size -- JSON Schema cannot compare two sibling field VALUES against each other within one object.

stringRecord.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.StringRecord.to_dict() -- one extracted string from a --strings scan or a --report triage card's own Section 4 (notable_strings). `offset` is a plain byte offset relative to the read region's start, NOT a process address. Unlike most other hexAddress-typed fields in this schema, `address` is never null -- a string was found at some real address, there is no "address unknown" case for it (see StringRecord.__post_init__). `matched_grep` is a flag, not a filter: this record is emitted for every extracted string regardless of --grep -- null when no --grep was given at all (always null for --report's own notable_strings, which has no --grep concept), true/false per record when it was.

stringsSummary.description: Matches result.summary for kind == 'strings' (dumpex.commands.extract.collect_strings). Pins the scan-context fields the P2 review's own 'a zero-result scan must still be able to tell where the scan started' finding needs machine-enforced, not just documented/unit-tested -- requested_address is the only way to know the scan origin when `data.records` is empty. additionalProperties: false since these six fields are the whole of collect_strings' own summary dict today; a future field added there must extend this def too, the same way every other v2 record type is kept in lockstep with its Python producer.

reportThreadInfo.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.ReportThreadInfo.to_dict() -- one thread as seen by --report, either the card's own anchor thread (Section 1) or one of the other threads sharing the anchor's resolved region (Section 3). `module_context` is null only when `start_address` is itself null (no address to resolve against). `backing_module_base`/`backing_module_end` are both-or-neither, and only ever non-null when `module_context == 'resolved'` -- Section 3's own 'other threads' entries never populate a range even when resolved (see the class's own docstring).

reportRegionInfo.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.ReportRegionInfo.to_dict() -- the memory region resolved at a triage card's target address (Section 2). `file_offset` is a plain byte offset inside the .dmp file, not a process address, so it does NOT use hexAddress. `module_context`/`mz_header_detected`/`has_injected_pe` are a tri-state triple: `module_context` is never null (a resolved region always has SOME module-context answer); `mz_header_detected` is null iff the small header-peek read itself failed; `has_injected_pe` is null whenever the evidence needed to decide is itself missing (see the class's own docstring for the full derivation table, mirrored in the allOf below).

reportIocString.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.ReportIocString.to_dict() -- one IOC-pattern string hit in a triage card's Section 4. `context_hex`/`context_base_address`/`context_hit_offset` are only ever populated when `is_network_pattern` is true -- a bounded (<=256 byte, i.e. <=512 hex char, enforced via context_hex's own maxLength) collect-time-computed hexdump-context window the renderer decodes instead of re-reading the dump (see dumpex.commands.report.render_report_console's own docstring for why). context_hit_offset's maximum of 255 is the loosest static bound this schema can express (the real constraint -- must fall strictly within THIS instance's own, possibly shorter, context_hex -- compares two sibling field values and is Python-only, see ReportIocString.__post_init__).

triageCardRecord.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.TriageCardRecord.to_dict() -- one --report triage card. --report-string produces N cards (one per private-memory hit region) in one result.data.records list; --report-tid/--report-addr produce exactly one. `findings` is a closed, deduplicated vocabulary; `verdict` is cross-checked against len(findings) via the allOf below (0/1/2/3+ -> CLEAN/SUSPICIOUS/LIKELY_MALICIOUS/HIGH_CONFIDENCE_MALICIOUS), the same four-tier rule dumpex.core.memory.verdict_for() enforces in Python. NOT expressed here (Python-only, see TriageCardRecord.__post_init__): string_scan['truncated'] must equal bytes_read < requested_bytes, and findings/finding_details must name exactly the same keys -- JSON Schema cannot compare two sibling field VALUES against each other within one object.

reportSummary.description: Matches result.summary for kind == 'report' (dumpex.commands.report.collect_report). `mode` says which of --report-tid/--report-addr/--report-string (or the tid+addr combination) produced this result -- the allOf below pins which query_* fields are required non-null per mode, the same way stringsSummary pins requested_address for --strings. `skipped_unreadable_regions`/`truncated_regions`/`clamped_regions` are StringSearchStats' own three counters (see dumpex.core.memory.StringSearchStats), always 0 outside string-search mode. additionalProperties: false since these twelve fields are the whole of collect_report's own summary dict today.

moduleDiffRecord.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.ModuleDiffRecord.to_dict() -- one added/removed/rebased module between two dumps, grounded in dumpex.commands.diff.diff_modules' own set logic. `name` is always a non-empty string ("(unnamed)" for an anonymous module -- see dumpex.commands.comparison._module_display_name), but full_path_before/full_path_after are only forced null on the side that genuinely has no entry -- the PRESENT side's full_path may legitimately be null too (an anonymous module has a real base_address but no name at all), so only base_address is required non-null for added/removed. `full_path_before`/`full_path_after` are otherwise unconstrained by change_type: address identifies a module diff, not path. NOT expressed here (Python-only, see ModuleDiffRecord.__post_init__): for `change_type: "rebased"`, base_address_before must differ from base_address_after -- JSON Schema cannot compare two sibling field VALUES for inequality within one object.

threadDiffRecord.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.ThreadDiffRecord.to_dict() -- one added/removed thread between two dumps, grounded in dumpex.commands.diff.diff_threads' own TID-keyed set logic. backing_module_after/backing_module_context are only ever populated for 'added' (resolved against the TARGET's module list); diff_threads never attempts baseline-side module resolution for a removed thread. For 'added': backing_module_after/backing_module_context are both null exactly when start_address_after itself is null (module resolution is never attempted without a known address); otherwise backing_module_context is always one of resolved/unregistered/unavailable, and backing_module_after is non-null iff backing_module_context is 'resolved'.

memoryDiffRecord.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.MemoryDiffRecord.to_dict() -- one added/removed/protection-changed memory region between two dumps, grounded in dumpex.commands.diff.diff_memory's own BaseAddress-keyed set logic. suspicious_before/_after reuse memoryRegionRecord.suspicious's own semantics rather than diff_memory's own 4-tier console categorization. NOT expressed here (Python-only, see MemoryDiffRecord.__post_init__): for `change_type: "protection_changed"`, protect_before must differ from protect_after -- JSON Schema cannot compare two sibling field VALUES for inequality within one object.

comparisonRecord.description: Tagged union for result.kind == 'comparison' -- discriminated by entity_type, which is a distinct const on each branch.

kind.description: Which canonical record type result.data.records holds. Grows as more commands migrate onto v2 -- not an open string.

execution_status.description: Did the COMMAND itself run to completion -- independent of whether the EVIDENCE it saw was complete (see coverage below). 'partial' is used by --report when a self-imposed scan-budget clamp (MAX_REGION_READ) or a per-card --output write failure means the command didn't finish everything it set out to do, even though the evidence it DID look at may be fully covered.

status.description: Was the evidence available to this command complete? Vocabulary shared with dumpex.hunt._coverage.derive_coverage_status.

reasons.description: Backward-compatible flat human text, rendered from `limitations` -- kept so an existing consumer that only reads `reasons` never breaks.

sources.description: Per-source observed state -- keyed by source name (e.g. 'memory_info', 'threads', or a dotted entity-namespaced name such as 'baseline.modules' for a comparison result). Optional: an older producer that doesn't populate this is still a valid document.

limitations.description: Structured, machine-readable coverage gaps -- the source `reasons` is rendered from. `code` is intentionally a plain string, not a closed enum: dumpex.output.coverage.LimitationCode grows as commands migrate, and this schema should not need a version bump every time a new code is added.

summary.description: Free-form per-kind extension point by default (open object) -- refined per-kind via the allOf/if-then block below exactly like data.records is, wherever a kind's own summary fields carry machine-relevant facts (e.g. kind == 'strings'/'report', whose requested_address/query_* fields are the only way to know a zero-result scan's own origin).

diagnosticEntry.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.Diagnostic.to_dict(), which always emits all three fields -- `code` is required (it's always a key in the dict), just nullable.

sourceObservation.description: Matches dumpex.output.coverage.SourceObservation.to_dict(), which always emits all three fields -- `required` covers all of them, not just `state`, and the record_count<->state invariant (None for absent/failed, exactly 0 for present_empty, >=1 for present) is frozen structurally below, mirroring the same invariant SourceObservation.__post_init__ enforces in Python.

scanTarget.description: Matches dumpex.output.coverage.ScanTarget.to_dict() -- ONE region/segment a scan did not examine, carried on a coverage limitation (coverageLimitation.targets) so a partial result names the exact virtual addresses an investigator still has to extract, rescan, or recollect rather than only counting them. New in schema_version 2.8. `size_limit` is the configured per-target cap this target exceeded, recorded per target because the same physical region can exceed several scan layers' different caps; WHICH layer is named once by the owning limitation's own `scope`, not repeated onto every target. As of schema_version 2.12, `size_limit` is `null` for a target that was never actually oversized -- a region a scan attempted but failed to read, read short, or ran out of scan budget on (there is no cap being exceeded there, just an I/O failure or a budget exhaustion); it stays non-null only for an oversized-skip target. `file_offset` is a byte offset inside the .dmp file (null when those bytes were never captured), NOT an address -- addresses use the fixed-width hexAddress form. allocation_base/state/type/protection are MemoryInfo facts and are always null for kind == "memory_segment", which has no MemoryInfo behind it. `captured_size`/`capture_state` (new in schema_version 2.12, issue #28) are a STRUCTURAL fact from the dump's own segment table -- how many of `size` bytes starting at `base_address` are actually present in the .dmp file, independent of whether any hunt's own live-memory read attempt succeeded. `capture_state` is derived from `captured_size` (`null` when not computed, `"none"` when 0, `"complete"` when equal to `size`, `"partial"` otherwise) -- see `investigationAction.evidence_availability`'s own `"partial"` value, which this field feeds. Python additionally requires size > size_limit whenever size_limit is non-null (a target that fits inside the cap was not skipped for being oversized), and captured_size <= size -- both comparisons between two field VALUES, which JSON Schema cannot express.

allOf.description: capture_state is derived from captured_size -- null iff captured_size is null.

coverageLimitation.description: Matches dumpex.output.coverage.CoverageLimitation.to_dict(), which always emits every field regardless of `code` (null/[] where a given code doesn't use a field) -- `required` covers the full set for the same reason sourceObservation's does. `allOf` below constrains each KNOWN code's disallowed fields to their default (null/[]), pins `source` where fixed, and mirrors the value-shape rules dumpex.output.coverage._CODE_SPECS/CoverageLimitation.__post_init__ enforce that JSON Schema CAN express (minItems, exact array contents, non-null requirements, one-field-implies-another-field dependencies) -- each `if` matches only that one `code` value, so an unrecognized future code matches none of them and stays fully open; `code` itself remains a plain string, not an enum. This is NOT full parity with the Python model: rules comparing two field VALUES for inequality (source != counterpart_source) or against another object's state entirely outside this fragment (counterpart_source's own record_count, a sibling entry in result.coverage.sources) are Python-only and cannot be expressed here -- see CoverageLimitation.__post_init__ and _validate_source_absent_against_sources for those, and, new in schema_version 2.8, SCAN_REGION_OVERSIZED_SKIPPED's own affected_count == len(targets) rule (a count compared against another field's array LENGTH, which JSON Schema cannot express either). Also new in 2.8: four source-keyed branches on SCAN_REGION_OVERSIZED_SKIPPED pin `scope` and every `targets[*].kind` to the fixed contract each known source (`pipe_name_scan`/`ioc_string_scan`/`segment_scan`/`encoding_scan`) actually produces -- mirroring dumpex.output.coverage._SCAN_REGION_OVERSIZED_SKIPPED_SOURCE_CONTRACTS; an unrecognized future `source` value matches none of the four and stays unconstrained on this axis, same as an unrecognized `code`.

targets.description: New in schema_version 2.8. The typed region/segment references a scan-coverage code identifies as the exact things it did not examine. Empty for every code that does not use it -- an existing consumer that ignores this key sees v2.7's shape unchanged. SCAN_REGION_OVERSIZED_SKIPPED always populates it (non-empty, length equals affected_count exactly). As of schema_version 2.12, PE_HEADER_READ_FAILED/PE_HEADER_SHORT_READ/PE_HEADER_SCAN_TRUNCATED/PE_HEADER_SCAN_NOT_STARTED/SCAN_REGION_READ_FAILED/SCAN_REGION_SHORT_READ may also populate it -- OPTIONAL on these six (a producer that cannot resolve target identity still emits `[]`), but when non-empty its length must equal affected_count exactly, same rule as SCAN_REGION_OVERSIZED_SKIPPED (Python-side rule, see the $def description above).

budget_limit.description: New in schema_version 2.12 (issue #28 P6 follow-up). The structured counterpart of `scope` naming WHICH resource budget a scan-budget-exhaustion code stopped on -- `scope` carries the (closed-vocabulary, per-code) KIND, this and `budget_consumed` carry that budget's own configured limit and how much was consumed. Kept as its own dedicated field rather than packed into `detail` (a prior version of this feature parsed "limit=<int> consumed=<int>" text out of `detail`, which broke the moment a code that ALSO uses `detail` for its own free-text reason -- e.g. CS_BEACON_SCAN_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED's human-readable budget_reason -- needed both at once). Minimum 0 (not 1) -- a configured budget of exactly 0 is legal (e.g. "no validations at all"). Non-null only alongside a non-null `scope`.

budget_consumed.description: Always equal to budget_limit when set (a budget is only ever attributed once fully consumed) -- kept as its own field, not derived, so a consumer never has to assume the two always agree. Minimum 0, same reasoning as budget_limit.

allOf.description: New in schema_version 2.12 (issue #28): the six read-failed/short-read/scan-truncated/scan-not-started codes are never oversized-skip codes, so a target attached to one of them can never carry the size_limit an oversized skip would have exceeded -- mirrors dumpex.output.coverage._require_optional_targets_matching_count's own Python-side size_limit check.

New in schema_version 2.12 (issue #28 P4/P6 follow-up): PE_HEADER_SCAN_TRUNCATED/PE_HEADER_SCAN_NOT_STARTED may optionally name WHICH of the hidden-PE scan's four independent budgets (reads_per_region/total_bytes/validations_per_region/validations_total -- see dumpex.hunt.injection.memory_scan._ScanBudget) stopped the region(s) this limitation reports, via `scope`, with that budget's own configured limit/consumed as `budget_limit`/`budget_consumed`. `null` together when no region in this hunt run's scan actually stopped on a budget. Mirrors dumpex.output.coverage._validate_optional_budget_fields -- the Python-only rule that scope and budget_limit/budget_consumed must be set TOGETHER (never one without the other) is not expressible here, same acknowledged gap this $def's own top-level description already notes for other cross-field rules.

New in schema_version 2.12 (issue #28 P6 follow-up): YARA_HIT_CAP_REACHED/YARA_SCAN_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED may optionally name WHICH of yara_hunt.scanner's own independent budgets (max_total_hits/scan_deadline_seconds/max_total_bytes_scanned) stopped the scan, via `scope`, with that budget's own configured limit/consumed as `budget_limit`/`budget_consumed`.

New in schema_version 2.12 (issue #28 P6 follow-up): CS_BEACON_SCAN_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED may optionally name WHICH of cs_beacon.scanner's own independent budgets (scan_deadline_seconds/max_total_scanned_bytes/max_candidates/max_decoded_bytes/max_hits) stopped the scan, via `scope`, with that budget's own configured limit/consumed as `budget_limit`/`budget_consumed` -- a SEPARATE fact from `detail`, which keeps its own pre-existing free-text human-readable reason on this code.

New in schema_version 2.12 (issue #28 P6 follow-up): every OTHER code (besides the five above) must leave budget_limit/budget_consumed null -- only a scan-budget-exhaustion code has a resource budget to attribute. Deliberately does NOT also constrain `scope` here -- unlike budget_limit/budget_consumed (which only these five codes ever use), `scope` has its own separate, established meanings on several OTHER codes entirely (e.g. SCAN_REGION_OVERSIZED_SKIPPED/SCAN_REGION_READ_FAILED/_SHORT_READ's own scan-layer name), each already constrained by its own dedicated branch elsewhere in this $def.

artifact.description: An output file the tool itself produced (e.g. an extracted memory region) -- distinct from meta.evidence, which describes the INPUT dump(s). Populated by --extract and --report (its own optional extract-to-file side effect, under a different `kind` string -- 'extracted_region' vs 'report_extracted_region'). Matches dumpex.output.records.Artifact.to_dict(), which always emits all six fields -- `required` covers all of them, not just id/kind/path.

finding.description: Matches dumpex.hunt._finding.Finding.to_dict() -- one hunter-agnostic judgment (facts/inference/confidence/rationale/limitations, tagged observation/lead/detection) inside a hunterRecord's `findings` array, extended (v2.5) with a normalized-SIEM-alert shape: `id` (deterministic -- 128-bit SHA-256 prefix of an unambiguous JSON encoding of check/rule_id/confidence/facts, so it never changes across a re-scan of the SAME evidence; content-only, so it is NOT a globally unique cross-dump identifier -- combine it with meta.evidence[].sha256 for that), `severity` (always derived from tag+confidence -- see the allOf block below, which pins the exact mapping so an external producer must follow it too, not just this codebase's own Finding.__post_init__), `technique_ids` (real MITRE ATT&CK technique/sub-technique IDs only, e.g. "T1055"/"T1559.001" -- empty unless the hunter has an actual mapping -- never invented per check), `evidence_refs` (structured pointers into the hunter's own `details`, distinct from free-text `facts`), `iocs` (indicator-of-compromise values), and `rule_id`/`rule_version` (detection-logic provenance -- `rule_id` defaults to `check`; `rule_version` stays null unless a real versioned rule source produced this finding, e.g. rules.yaml-derived findings carry that ruleset's own CONTENT sha256, never rules.yaml's top-level `version:` FORMAT field, which does not change when rule content does). yara is the one hunter that never populates this -- its own matches/rules_hit stay in YaraDetails instead (see hunterRecord's own allOf: findings must be [] for hunter == 'yara').

id.description: Matches dumpex.hunt._finding.Finding's own "finding-" + 32 lowercase hex chars (128-bit SHA-256 prefix) shape exactly -- pattern PLUS an exact minLength/maxLength, same reasoning as technique_ids' own two-branch shape above (a bare '^...$' pattern alone would accept a trailing-newline-appended value one character too long).

items.description: MITRE ATT&CK technique ("T1055") or sub-technique ("T1559.001") id. Expressed as two fixed-length oneOf branches, each pattern PLUS an exact minLength/maxLength, rather than a single '^...$'-anchored pattern -- a review found that '$' (in both Python re, which the `jsonschema` library's own pattern check uses via re.search(), AND in ECMA 262, the dialect the JSON Schema spec itself designates) matches just before a trailing newline, not only at the true end of string, so a bare pattern alone would incorrectly accept "T1055\n"/"T1559.001\n". The length bound closes that gap portably, without relying on a non-standard anchor like Python's \Z.

allOf.description: severity is a pure function of (tag, confidence) -- see dumpex.hunt._finding.severity_for()'s own 9-entry mapping table. Pinned here as an allOf/if-then so a producer OTHER than this codebase's own Finding dataclass cannot emit a document where severity contradicts tag+confidence -- the same enforcement Finding.__post_init__ applies in Python (severity is init=False there), now also enforced on the wire.

huntRegionRef.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.HuntRegionRef.to_dict() -- a memory region reference inside a hunter's `details`, replacing the raw Region object v1.1 exposed via `_json_safe()`'s non-reproducible str(obj) fallback (see docs/hunt_migration_field_matrix.md's cross-cutting finding #1). `base_address` is never null -- a region reference always names a real address.

huntThreadRef.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.HuntThreadRef.to_dict() -- a TID plus optional StartAddress/current-instruction-pointer, hex-formatted. `ip`/`ip_reg` are both-or-neither: a thread reference either carries no live register snapshot (both null) or a real one (both set) -- there is no case where the register name is known but its value isn't, or vice versa.

huntThreadRegionHit.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.HuntThreadRegionHit.to_dict() -- a thread correlated with a specific region, e.g. a thread's current RIP/EIP executing inside a flagged allocation, or its StartAddress falling inside one.

huntPeHeaderHit.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.HuntPeHeaderHit.to_dict() -- one MZ candidate examined for a hidden PE header: where it is, its containing region, and the structural-validation outcome. `entry_point_rva` stays a plain int (an RVA is relative to a not-yet-established image base, not itself a memory address); `image_base` (the PE header's OWN declared base) is a real address, hex-formatted. `reason` is set only when `valid` is false; every PE-fact field is set only when `valid` is true. New in schema_version 2.11: `va` (the process address the candidate's 'MZ' was found at), `region_offset` (how far into `region` that is) and `file_offset` (where those bytes sit in the .dmp, `null` when the VA is not covered by any captured segment -- not the same claim as offset zero). The hidden-PE scan searches whole regions for candidates rather than only probing each region base, so `region` alone no longer identifies where a PE actually is; for a PE at a region's base `va` equals `region.base_address` and `region_offset` is 0.

injectionDetails.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.InjectionDetails.to_dict() -- `--hunt injection`'s hunter-specific evidence. `pe_read_failed`/`pe_short_reads` deliberately do NOT appear here -- those are coverage counts, not evidence (see PE_HEADER_READ_FAILED/PE_HEADER_SHORT_READ limitations under this hunter's own coverage instead).

hollowingDetails.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.HollowingDetails.to_dict() -- `--hunt hollowing`'s hunter-specific evidence: the four checks (memory type / MZ header / RWX protection at the image base, and the PEB-vs-module-list name compare). Unlike the other six hunters, every field here is a scalar -- all fields are scalar. `image_base` is null exactly when the PEB itself is missing (this hunter's NOT_EVALUATED case) -- there is no image base to report at all, unlike every other hunter's details, which always have SOME evidence even under incomplete coverage.

stompingDetails.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.StompingDetails.to_dict() -- `--hunt stomping`'s hunter-specific evidence. `protection_leads`/`verified_changes` entries are plain objects, not yet a dedicated typed shape (tracked follow-up -- see docs/hunt_migration_field_matrix.md's stomping section) -- open objects here reflect that Python-side reality rather than inventing a contract the collector doesn't enforce yet.

pipeDetails.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.PipeDetails.to_dict() -- `--hunt pipe`'s hunter-specific evidence. Entries are plain objects, not yet a dedicated typed shape (tracked follow-up) -- same rationale as stompingDetails above.

csBeaconDetails.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.CsBeaconDetails.to_dict() -- `--hunt cs-beacon`'s hunter-specific evidence. NOT expressed here (Python-only, see CsBeaconDetails.__post_init__): config_count must equal len(configs). As of schema_version 2.7, each `configs[*]` item's `fields` is keyed by field NAME (e.g. `"BeaconType"`, or `"field_0xNNNN"` for an unrecognized field ID) instead of the raw TLV field ID string, and each field's own value carries only `type`/`value` -- the `name` property (redundant once the key IS the name) was dropped (see dumpex/hunt/cs_beacon/collect.py's `_config_dict()`/`_field_dict()`). Unlike the `raw`-removal in 2.6, THIS constraint IS expressed structurally below (`fields`' own `propertyNames`/`additionalProperties`), not just documented -- a `configs[*]` item whose `fields` still uses numeric-string keys or still carries a `name` property fails validation. `configs[*]` items otherwise stay schema-open (`type: object`) here -- every property besides `fields` is unconstrained.

fields.description: Keyed by field NAME (schema_version 2.7) -- a purely-numeric-string key (the pre-2.7 shape) is rejected by propertyNames below.

yaraDetails.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.YaraDetails.to_dict() -- `--hunt yara`'s hunter-specific evidence. Deliberately off the shared `finding` model -- a YARA rule hit is a structural pattern match, not a check/facts/inference/confidence/rationale judgment.

obfuscationDetails.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.ObfuscationDetails.to_dict() -- `--hunt obfuscation`'s hunter-specific evidence: the seven decode layers' own hit lists.

hunterRecord.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.HunterRecord.to_dict() -- one hunter's complete result, one entry in `result.data.records` for `result.kind == "hunt"`. `hunter` discriminates which of the 7 *Details types `details` must be (see the allOf below). `max_score`/`confidence`/`lead_count`/`review_priority` are null for every hunter except `hunter == "yara"`, where they must ALL be null -- never a mix of some set, some not (yara has none of these today, see docs/hunt_migration_field_matrix.md's yara section). `coverage` is this ONE hunter's own CoverageReport, not the top-level `result.coverage` (which combines all selected hunters' reports -- see combine_coverage_reports()).

huntSummary.description: Matches result.summary for kind == 'hunt' -- the cross-hunter roll-up a single shared reducer computes (never re-derived independently by JSON/console -- see docs/hunt_migration_field_matrix.md's own summary-rules section). `selected` is the `--hunt` argument ("all" or one hunter name). `highest_verdict_level` is picked only from DETECTED hunters when any exist; otherwise it reflects the strongest non-detected signal (clean/inconclusive/not_evaluated).

skipRelationship.description: Matches dumpex.hunt._investigation.SkipRelationship.to_dict() -- one (hunter, source, scope, cause) that skipped this physical target. `source`/`scope` mirror the owning coverageLimitation's own fields (source stays an open vocabulary, same as coverageLimitation.source). `cause` is new in schema_version 2.12 -- `hunter`/`source`/`scope` alone cannot distinguish an oversized region a scan never attempted from one it attempted and failed to read, read short, or ran out of scan budget on. `size_limit` is non-null only when `cause` is `"oversized_skipped"` (the cap that target exceeded); every other cause leaves it `null`, since there is no cap being exceeded for an I/O failure or a scan-budget exhaustion.

budget_kind.description: New in schema_version 2.12 (issue #28 P5 follow-up). WHICH of injection's four independent hidden-PE scan budgets (reads_per_region/total_bytes/validations_per_region/validations_total) this relationship's own scan_truncated/scan_not_started stopped on -- the structured counterpart of what previously only reached `scope` (see coverageLimitation's own PE_HEADER_SCAN_TRUNCATED/_SCAN_NOT_STARTED scope/detail wiring). `null` for every other cause.

budget_limit.description: That budget's own configured limit, or null when budget_kind is null. Minimum 0 (not 1) -- a configured budget of exactly 0 is legal (e.g. "no validations at all").

budget_consumed.description: Always equal to budget_limit when set (a budget is only ever attributed once fully consumed) -- kept as its own field, not derived, so a consumer never has to assume the two always agree. Minimum 0, same reasoning as budget_limit.

allOf.description: New in schema_version 2.12 (issue #28 P5 follow-up): budget_kind/budget_limit/budget_consumed are only ever set together for cause scan_truncated/scan_not_started; every other cause leaves all three null. (The Python-side rule that budget_consumed always equals budget_limit is a cross-field VALUE comparison and is not expressible here -- see coverageLimitation's own $def description for this schema's general stance on that class of rule.)

contentFinding.description: Matches dumpex.hunt._investigation.ContentFinding.to_dict() -- one piece of structured evidence the opt-in --triage-skipped deep read itself found (issue #19 Phase 2), backing the quick triage.content_reason_codes summary with actual detail. `type` discriminates two closed, mutually exclusive shapes: 'ioc_string' (offset/encoding/value/is_network_pattern all set, module_context null -- value is truncated to at most 256 characters, a bounded lead rather than the full match) and 'mz_header' (module_context set, every ioc_string-only field null). At most 20 of these accompany one investigationAction entry (triageInfo.findings' own maxItems) -- an analyst who needs the complete string text, hexdump context, or an extractable artifact still runs --report --report-addr <target.base_address> directly; this array is a bounded lead, never a substitute.

triageInfo.description: Matches dumpex.hunt._investigation.TriageInfo.to_dict(). The --hunt all default pass only ever emits mode == "metadata", pinned to status == "completed", bytes_examined == 0, region_fully_examined == false, content_reason_codes == [], findings == [], finding_count == 0, findings_truncated == false -- the schema-enforced proof that the default pass never reads region content. mode == "deep" is emitted by the opt-in --hunt all --triage-skipped budgeted deep-content triage pass (dumpex.hunt._deep_triage.run_deep_triage(), issue #19 Phase 2): status in [not_captured, budget_deferred, unreadable] means no read was attempted/succeeded (bytes_examined == 0, region_fully_examined == false, content_reason_codes == [], findings == [], finding_count == 0, findings_truncated == false -- no content signal is possible without a real read); status == completed means the whole target was examined (region_fully_examined == true) and bytes_examined >= 1; status in [partial, clamped] means bytes_examined >= 1 but the target was NOT fully examined (region_fully_examined == false) -- partial is a real evidence gap (the dump had fewer bytes than requested), clamped is deep triage's own per-target/run-budget policy limit. content_reason_codes/findings are populated only for completed/partial/clamped, from `_scan_content_range()`'s own IOC-pattern/network-pattern string matches and MZ-header detection over the bytes actually examined -- content_reason_codes is a quick, closed-vocabulary SUMMARY; findings (see the contentFinding $def, capped at 20 entries) is the bounded, structured EVIDENCE backing it, selected REPRESENTATIVE-FIRST (an MZ finding, then one network-pattern IOC finding, then one plain IOC finding, then remaining IOC findings in offset order) rather than a bare offset-order fill, so a reason code is never left with zero backing evidence purely because 20+ plain IOC hits filled every slot first. finding_count is the TOTAL number of individual findings this read produced (BEFORE that capped/reordered selection -- an MZ header counts as at most 1, every IOC string hit counts as 1 each); findings_truncated is true exactly when finding_count > len(findings), i.e. the array does not carry every finding the read produced. MZ_HEADER_DETECTED and INJECTED_PE_HEADER are independent facts, not one collapsed code: MZ_HEADER_DETECTED means the read's own start begins with an MZ header; INJECTED_PE_HEADER additionally requires that memory be CONFIRMED unregistered (module classification available and no owning module found) -- when module classification itself is unavailable (no ModuleListStream in this dump), that confirmation cannot be made, and MZ_HEADER_DETECTED alone still surfaces the raw signal rather than silently dropping it. content_reason_codes/findings are never a verdict, and never a claim that the originating hunter's own coverage gap (see investigationAction.coverage_effect) is resolved.

recommendedAction.description: Matches dumpex.hunt._investigation.RecommendedAction.to_dict(). `hunters` is present only on type == "targeted_hunter_rescan".

investigationAction.description: Matches dumpex.hunt._investigation.InvestigationAction.to_dict() -- one deduplicated physical skipped target (see build_investigation_queue()'s own docstring for the dedup key), with every hunter/source/scope that skipped it merged into `skipped_by`. `priority`/`evidence_availability` are two independent axes: a missing captured range means recollection may be needed, never that the target is more suspicious. `coverage_effect` is always "original_hunter_gap_not_resolved" in this schema version -- only a real hunter-specific targeted rescan (not implemented yet) could ever change it.
